# ARKhives 8.18.0 — clearer reviewing, automatic ARKLeague and account management

## Where to find the changes
- **My Reviewers:** tap MCQs or Flashcards to choose a session; use the small settings icon for advanced reviewer details.
- **Profile → Change username:** saves to the same account; progress stays attached.
- **ARKLeague:** choose a public identity once. Joined accounts update automatically from saved progress.
- **Administration → Accounts:** search/filter accounts, open the three-dot details panel, then choose the required action. Permanent deletion is master-admin only.
- **Administration → Content Review Studio:** filter the reviewer/status, edit an item, then use **Save edits** or **Reviewed & next**. AI proposals are suggestions to review before saving.
- **Learning & sync → Compare sync copies:** use this when a conflict requires a recovery choice; both originals are backed up first.

## Reviewer cards and mobile navigation
- MCQs and Flashcards have separate slides with direct session setup. The small settings icon opens advanced reviewer details.
- Mode dots, desktop arrows and mobile swipes are supported. Automatic sliding pauses during interaction, dialogs and study, and respects reduced motion.
- Cards distinguish due reviews from new flashcards, and show MCQ unseen/repair counts.
- Mobile keeps Home, Reviewers, Progress and Profile in its dock. Saved Questions, Achievements, ARKLeague and ARKbot remain in the side menu.

## The four reported mobile study problems
- Phone exam questions use the full available width instead of a narrow right column. The question comes before the bounded exam overview/workpad.
- Flashcard text uses the available card face, with its own scroll for long answers. Rating controls stay outside that scrolling area.
- Long saved explanations and AI guidance use separate bounded reading surfaces, keeping content above the bottom controls.
- Recall guidance is initially collapsed on phones. The small loading logo no longer inherits the study image size.
- Missing saved explanations show a clear empty state and retain the same reading-panel structure.

## ARKLeague on desktop and mobile
- Participation updates automatically from committed cloud progress while the signed-in app is open and online; no manual score-sync action is needed. Checks normally run every 45 seconds and back off after failures.
- The server derives distinct daily participation and the chosen built-in companion from the account's saved snapshot. Unchanged cloud revisions skip score writes.
- Participation remains opt-in. Custom companion artwork needs explicit desktop consent; only a 96×96 thumbnail is public. Changing away from that custom companion removes its public thumbnail on the next saved-progress update.
- Public custom thumbnails render as verified PNG images instead of being rejected by the built-in sprite loader. Accounts without an explicit companion now use the same avatar fallback on mobile and desktop.
- Public artwork is requested in batches rather than one request per learner. Standings use consistent trophy icons, clearer personal position and a compact responsive layout.
- Participation scores are not proctored exam results or a readiness prediction.

## Accounts and administration
- Update desktop and mobile to this matching release before changing a username. Older desktop builds do not support renamed accounts.
- Signed-in users can change their username from Profile. The cloud checks uniqueness ignoring case. Previous names remain reserved to the account while it exists.
- Desktop keeps a stable account progress key through renames, retaining schedules, notes, appearance and custom companion ownership.
- Administration uses its own sidebar with account/content/review/integration/history sections and Back to ARKhives.
- Master admins get a paginated account directory with search, status/role filters, summary counts and a details panel. Activation, reactivation, access changes and private password-setup codes remain available.
- Only master admins can permanently delete another non-master account. Deletion requires its email and explicit confirmation; the server verifies the target again and disables cloud access before deletion. Founder/master and self-deletion are blocked here.
- Cloud account removal does not erase files held by disconnected desktops. Shared reviewer content is retained. No real accounts were deleted in acceptance testing.
- The directory reads only an explicit safe field list through one paginated database query; passwords, hashes and private authentication metadata are never returned.

## Additional sync correction
- A reset of a card or entire subject now checks the original device/cloud records before merging. A simultaneous review cannot disappear merely because the reset removed the card from the merged list. Both copies require an explicit recovery choice. Uncontested and matching resets remain valid.

## Verification and remaining limits
- Tests cover protected deletion and failure handling using synthetic accounts, authenticated database permission/rename checks with rolled-back fixtures, native identity preservation, editor/account UI interaction, and phone exam/long-card layouts in Chromium and WebKit.
- The backend security advisor still reports leaked-password protection disabled. Existing server-only tables intentionally deny direct client reads; that is not an exposed-data warning. See https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/password-security#password-strength-and-leaked-password-protection for the remaining Auth option.
- Forced CDP freezing did not resume this PWA reliably in the installed Chrome harness; acceptance uses actual tab discard/reopen plus ordinary offline reload. Physical suspension remains unverified.
- Physical iPhone/iPad, actual two-monitor dragging and a user's real account session require device acceptance; browser simulation is not reported as physical-device testing.
